review_notes:
I read all of Geometry.lean (lines 1–106). I also read the definitions it depends on in Sobolev/Basic.lean (testCls, partialCls, testGraph, the @[simp] lemmas testGraph_zero and testGraph_succ, and inner_toLp_eq). I read Analysis/L2Norm.lean and grepped for every use of the file's declarations.

The file adds no simp lemmas, no simp attributes and no simp sets. Its two bridge lemmas, norm_testGraph_zero_sq_eq and norm_testGraph_succ_sq_eq, are used only through explicit `rw` and `Finset.sum_congr` inside poincare_testfn. The rubric warns against adding @[simp] merely because an identity looks simple.

I found no clear gap in the simp interface:
- testGraph_zero and testGraph_succ are already @[simp], so the testGraph-to-testCls/partialCls normalisation is covered upstream. The `rw [IsTestFn.testGraph_zero]` calls in this file are deliberate and not a defect.
- Marking the bridge lemmas @[simp] would risk unwanted integral expansion. The lemmas have a norm-squared left-hand side and an integral right-hand side. Nothing in the sources shows that a simp normal form would help.
- I found no rewrite cycle and no competing rules. The `simp only [IsTestFn.testCls]` and `simp only [IsTestFn.partialCls]` calls are narrow unfoldings.

The only residual observation is stylistic and not a simp-interface defect. The proofs of the two bridge lemmas repeat the `real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq` and `inner_toLp_eq` pattern, which Analysis/L2Norm.lean already packages as norm_sq_L2_eq. I did not report it because it falls outside this rubric.

I could not run Lean, so I cannot rule out simp behaviour that depends on elaboration elsewhere in the library.
